title: A child task that loops without waiting is never stopped by its group's `deadline`.
text: `rule:concurrency/limit-and-deadline-are-the-only-bounds` makes `deadline` bound the whole call. `run_as_children` arms it as a timer on the core's reactor and reads the clock when the parent is resumed, and a child whose loop calls nothing never gives the core back, so neither happens: `Core\Task::all` over two `while (true)` bodies under `{deadline: 50ms}` runs until the process is killed. Safepoint polls reach the child, but the word they read is the request tree's (`nvs_runtime::ctx::safepoint`'s `TreeState`), so raising it would stop the whole request rather than one group, and the request's own `cpu_time` and `wall_time` default to no cap. Closing it needs a per-group or per-task stop that a poll can read, which is a representation change. No thread can raise that stop while the core spins except `nvs_host::watchdog`, which sweeps every 500 ms and whose module doc writes nothing on a request path for its benefit, so closing it as the rule reads needs a design record. The other answer is a rule change: `wall_time` only expires the word a member polls inside a long call (`nvs_runtime::abi`'s `deadline_passed`), so a request that never waits is bounded by `cpu_time` alone, and the rule could bound a never-waiting child the same way. Either one is the user's decision. `tests/hostile/core/Task/all/03-tasks-that-never-wait.nvs` carries this record's marker.
